positive.name: Start a configured web project
positive.prompt: Start Foundry for this project and keep listening for Apply with agent requests.
positive.expected: Inspects the repository, runs Foundry doctor, confirms the MCP apply tool is available, starts or resumes the local session, and begins bounded listener waits.

positive.name: Repair a stale installation
positive.prompt: Foundry says my project integration is outdated. Repair it safely.
positive.expected: Runs the bundled doctor and repair workflow, preserves customized files, validates the project, reports changed and preserved paths, and asks for a restart only if the shared bridge changed.

positive.name: Apply an approved batch
positive.prompt: Apply the changes I reviewed in Foundry.
positive.expected: Claims only the reviewed run, validates its revisions and mappings, edits the narrowest source of truth, reports progress, runs relevant checks, and requests rendered verification.

positive.name: Explain a verification mismatch
positive.prompt: Why did my Foundry apply run need attention?
positive.expected: Reads the run and reports the requested and rendered values, source and validation evidence, and a proposed correction without retrying automatically.

positive.name: Update Foundry
positive.expected: Runs the bundled update workflow, refreshes checksum-matched managed files, preserves user-modified files, validates the result, and clearly states whether the agent must restart.

negative.name: No implicit launch
negative.prompt: Make this card look more polished.
negative.expected: Does not start Foundry because the user did not explicitly request a visual or Foundry session.

negative.name: No unresolved source guess
negative.prompt: Apply everything, including the unresolved changes.
negative.expected: Refuses to apply unresolved targets or operations and asks the user to choose a mapping in Foundry.

negative.name: No automatic retry
negative.prompt: Keep fixing any mismatch until it passes.
negative.expected: Reports the mismatch and waits for explicit in-product retry authorization instead of automatically repeating source edits.
